A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGVC research, retaining its graph-consolidation pipeline and principal benchmarks despite a revised title and emphasis. All 13 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SGVC results on MSR-VTT and ActivityNet Captions, a frame-count ablation in Tables 1–3, and qualitative outputs.

after.justification: v2 reports original SGVC results on MSR-VTT, MSVD, and ActivityNet Captions, computational measurements, hyperparameter studies, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The caption-generation stage extends from individual frames processed by image VLMs to either frames or short clips, including an implemented InternVL2.5 configuration. This broadens the input procedure, while Hungarian object matching, graph consolidation, prioritized subgraph extraction, and the graph-to-text training objective remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds MSVD evaluation alongside retained MSR-VTT and ActivityNet Captions evaluations. The graph-to-text training sources remain the same. Long-video paragraph captioning already appeared in v1, so the revised long-video emphasis does not establish a newly added task.

E2.justification: v2 adds VidIL without reference exemplars, evaluates VidIL and Video ChatCaptioner on ActivityNet, and adds GPT-4o mini summarization. It removes ActivityNet comparisons with MFT, PDVC, Vid2Seq, and Streaming GIT, and drops DeCap-CC3M from MSR-VTT. Most other earlier MSR-VTT comparators remain in Appendix A, Table 8.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from LLaVA-based captions to comparisons across BLIP, BLIP2, and InternVL2.5 configurations, extending the existing same-caption summarization controls. Paragraph fine-tuning is reported as 400 rather than 500 iterations. New protocols measure per-video inference time and peak memory and vary graph hyperparameters; the retained captioning metrics and dataset splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The 4–12-frame ablation in v1 Table 3 is removed. v2 instead tests prioritized-subgraph size k and matching threshold tau in Tables 6–7, adds computational-cost analysis, and presents explicit counting and object-misidentification failures in Appendix C. Additional qualitative examples expand the diagnostic evidence beyond relocated examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetition counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The additional results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark, backbone, efficiency, and sensitivity results while removing the earlier frame-count and supervised ActivityNet results. In retained LLaVA-based MSR-VTT entries, SGVC FBERT changes from 0.484 to 0.497 and Mistral summarization FBERT from 0.416 to 0.414 without explanation (v1 Table 1; v2 Table 8). New-backbone results do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The scene-graph definitions, cosine/Hungarian matching, attribute union, next-token objective, and BERTScore mathematics retain their substance. Graph-update notation is shortened into Algorithm 1 and equations are renumbered, without a new theoretical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion redefine the central contribution from transferring image VLMs into zero-shot video captioning to extending both image and short-video models beyond their temporal windows for long-video captioning. Performance and efficiency claims now center on LLM-based consolidation, changing the claimed applicability and contribution framing.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that initial VLM counting and identification hallucinations propagate through consolidation. It adds interpretations of the k precision–recall trade-off and InternVL2.5's temporal-modeling benefits. Appendix A also strengthens the superiority interpretation to all evaluation metrics, although Table 8 still gives Mistral summarization higher METEOR than SGVC.

D1.justification: New disclosures include the 235M-parameter model, BERT-base and decoder-only T5-base, frame-sampling counts, k and tau defaults, paragraph repetition penalty, A6000 measurement hardware, and CPU graph merging. v1's explicit randomized LLaVA decoding recipe is omitted. Prompt templates and principal optimizer settings remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish corresponding changes to earlier experiments.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned around long-video consolidation, adding memory-based and recursive approaches such as memory consolidation, MovieChat, Video ReCap, and LongVLM, alongside newer video models and BLIP/BLIP2. This replaces the earlier paragraph-captioning-centered discussion and changes the comparison with prior research beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around long-video captioning. Method and experiment subsections are reorganized, analysis gains separate efficiency and hyperparameter discussions, and appendices are reordered and expanded. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond additions of scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with a graph-to-text attention-mask illustration. Results are reorganized into backbone- and dataset-grouped tables, with new efficiency and sensitivity displays and an expanded appendix comparison. Qualitative figures are enlarged, rearranged, and supplemented; several earlier examples and the prompt tables are retained through relocation.

improvement.justification: v1 claims efficiency and backbone flexibility without measured costs or evaluation across multiple backbones. v2 substantially strengthens this evidence through image/video backbone comparisons, stronger ActivityNet comparators, and measured memory and runtime in Table 5. Hyperparameter studies and explicit failure cases also improve assessability. Removing the frame-count ablation and supervised comparisons loses useful context, while unexplained BERTScore revisions and overbroad superiority wording weaken reporting. These drawbacks do not outweigh the substantial improvement in support for the paper's central claims.
